title: Companies, Monoliths, and Government
text: Zenith is governed by 24 Monoliths– corporations that have grown powerful enough to effectively become governments. Each Monolith controls one Zone along with a monopolized major industry. A Monolith controls the laws, infrastructure, resources, and services within its territory while also running its industry across Zenith. The 24 Monoliths together form The Conglomerate, which handles things that affect Zenith as a whole. CORPORATIONS Corporations make up the vast majority of Zenith's economy. They own businesses and property, employ people, provide goods and services, and compete with one another for just about everything worth having. Corporations operate with a considerable amount of freedom and independence average citizens do not have. But despite their power and ever-looming presence, Only Monoliths can have sovereignty over a Zone. Corporate conflicts are common. Companies may compete over resources, territory, contracts, technology, or influence. These conflicts can range from economic pressure and espionage to sabotage and even full on armed conflict. Most of the time, Monoliths leave corporations to deal with their own disputes, But they may step in if a conflict starts threatening infrastructure or their own interests. MONOLITHS A Monolith is a corporation that has become dominant enough to control an entire industry. There are 24 Monoliths in Zenith, each associated with a major industry. Their influence extends far beyond their base Zones, and most businesses operating within their industries ultimately have to deal with them. BioMedica, for example, is the health Monolith. Hospitals, pharmaceuticals, medical research, and other major medical services fall under its influence. Monoliths can license their technology and services to other companies, meaning not every business associated with a Monolith is directly owned by it. These companies are still expected to operate within the Monolith's rules. GOVERNING A ZONE Every Monolith has one singular Zone where its government is located. A Zone is, for all practical purposes, a country. Its Monolith controls the laws, taxes, infrastructure, public services, transportation, resources, and borders of the territory, etc. Most of these things are handled locally, meaning life can look very different from one Zone to another. A Monolith administers its Zone through its own departments and officials. The Monolith's CEO ultimately holds authority over both the corporation and its government. Owning land does not make a company a Monolith. The important difference is sovereignty. A corporation can own property within a Zone, but the Monolith decides what happens within the Zone itself. BECOMING A MONOLITH In theory, any corporation can become a Monolith. In practice, this means becoming powerful enough to dominate an industry and taking control of a Zone. Usually, this requires displacing an existing Monolith. This is extremely rare. Monoliths can remain in power for centuries, and replacing one is a major event for all of Zenith. RELATIONS BETWEEN MONOLITHS The Monoliths are competitors, but they can't afford to completely ignore one another. Every Zone depends on things produced somewhere else. Food might come from one Zone, medicine from another, and transportation may be controlled by a third. Keeping all of this moving requires the Monoliths to cooperate, even when they don't particularly like each other. But yet, they still get in each other's way. A Monolith might try to undercut another Monolith's business, interfere with its operations, or gain an advantage through the Conglomerate. Things can get considerably worse when their interests directly collide. Open warfare is uncommon. A fight between two Monoliths could disrupt entire industries and affect millions of people, so there is usually a reason to find another way. For the average person, the Monoliths are simply the powers that run Zenith. Which one you live under determines a surprising amount about your life. THE CONGLOMERATE The Conglomerate is the closest thing Zenith has to a central government. The Conglomerate handles matters that affect multiple Zones, maintains shared institutions, and establishes the relatively small number of laws that apply throughout Zenith. CONGLOMERATE LAWS Most laws in Zenith are decided at the Zone level. Criminal law, taxation, business regulations, licensing, and many other rules can vary from one Zone to another. Conglomerate law mainly covers matters that affect Zenith as a whole and rules that keep the Monoliths from completely tearing each other apart. Some of the most important Conglomerate laws include: Murder is prohibited. Theft is prohibited. Monoliths must respect each other's territorial sovereignty. No Monolith may claim or annex another Monolith's Zone. Conglomerate Institutions must be recognized throughout Zenith. Monoliths must abide by decisions made through the Conglomerate's voting process. These laws, despite being universal, aren't enforced very well. Enforcement varies between Zones, and Monoliths are can and will interfere with law enforcement when it suits them. INSTITUTIONS The Institutions are organizations maintained by The Conglomerate that operate across the Zones. Some of the more familiar ones are: The Gavel: Law enforcement. The Scale: Courts and the judicial system. The Ledger: Taxes and Conglomerate finances. The Registry: Legal and civil records. The Arm: Major disasters and emergencies. The Institutions are supposed to operate throughout Zenith, but they still have to work within territory controlled by a Monolith. A local branch can therefore find itself restricted or interfered with by the Monolith of the Zone it operates in. For most people, dealing with an Institution can feel very different depending on where they are.

title: Fixers
description: Dont wanna be a Corpo? Look no further!
text: Fixers are independent contractors hired to do jobs that someone else can't, won't, or doesn't want to deal with themselves. Fixers can work for pretty much anyone. Private citizens, businesses, Corporations, and even Monoliths will hire them when they need something done without putting their own people on the job. A Fixer's work can be completely legal, highly illegal, or somewhere in between depending on who's paying and where the job takes place. Most Fixers work for themselves and take jobs one at a time, although some form long-term partnerships or work as part of a larger group, known a Network. Common Fixer Jobs There's no real limit to what a Fixer can be hired to do. Some specialize in a particular kind of work, while others will take whatever pays. Some examples are, but not limited to: Couriers: Delivering packages, messages, or people. Runners: Moving illegal or restricted cargo between Zones, often through the Pale. Guards: Protecting people, property, or important cargo. Hunters: Tracking down wanted or missing people. Ghosts: Finding information, uncovering secrets, or locating people. Saboteurs: Disrupting businesses, damaging property, or getting in the way of a competitor. Cleaners: Getting rid of specific targets, usually for criminal or political clients. Mechanics: Repairing equipment, modifying technology, or dealing with systems other people can't figure out. Admins: Handling paperwork, finances, taxes, and other boring problems. FIXER NETWORKS Fixers don't always work alone. Many belong to Fixer Networks, loose organizations of Fixers who share contacts, resources, and jobs. Networks can be small groups of friends or large organizations with members spread across multiple Zones. Some are highly organized, with offices, rankings, and their own job boards, while others are little more than a and a list of people to call when a job comes up. Being part of a Network can make finding work much easier. A Fixer might take a job through their Network, pass it along to someone better suited for it, or call on another member when they need help. There's no single way to run a Network. Some are little more than professional associations, while others operate almost like guilds with their own rules, reputation, and internal hierarchy. Due to some Networks being officially recognized as Corporations, they are granted a lot more leniency with the law then a freelance or low grade fixer.

title: Signatures
text: SIGNATURES Signatures are rare 'living' weapons created from the cores of an old, powerful extinct species known as Moon Children. Each Signature possesses its own abilities and can form a permanent bond with a compatible human. A person bonded to a Signature is called a Signer. Due to its history, Signatures are wildly known to exist, but they are still extremely uncommon. Most people will never encounter one. Due to the Extinction of Moon Children in year 320, no more Signatures are capable of being created. THE BOND A Signature can only be wielded by someone it bonds with. What makes someone compatible isn't fully understood, although personality, experiences, and temperament seem to play a role. Once bonded, the human becomes a Signer. The Signature will refuse to work for anyone else, and its appearance may gradually change as its relationship with its Signer develops. The bond also gives Signers physical abilities beyond those of ordinary humans, such as increased strength, speed, endurance, and resilience. ABILITIES Every Signature has its own unique ability or set of related abilities. A Signer usually learns the most obvious uses first, with more advanced applications developing through experience and experimentation. No two Signatures are necessarily alike, and their abilities can vary dramatically. SIGNERS There are very few active Signers across Zenith. Some openly use their Signatures, while others keep them hidden to avoid attention from Monoliths and other Fixers, or anyone else interested in their abilities.

title: The Pale
text: The Pale is the name commonly given to the regions outside the Zones. It is not a single biome or uniformly barren wasteland, but a vast collection of natural environments ranging from relatively ordinary wilderness to extremely harsh and dense regions. Parts of the Pale can look surprisingly similar to the edges of nearby Zones. The difference becomes more apparent with distance, where larger expanses of wilderness, denser vegetation, unfamiliar wildlife, and other features of Zenith's native environment become increasingly common. The Pale can be extraordinarily beautiful, But is nevertheless dangerous for most unprepared and ordinary humans due to the of environmental conditions and biological hazards. Most Zenithans regard the Pale as inherently dangerous and unsuitable for permanent human habitation, the name itself even carrying negative connotations. For more information on Zenith, Refer to it's page.

title: Zenith
text: OVERVIEW Zenith is the planet humanity settled after abandoning Earth nearly 1,000 years ago. The planet is significantly different from Earth, with its own plants, animals, ecosystems, and geological processes. Humanity has spent centuries studying Zenith, but the majority of the planet's aspects remain barely understood. Most of humanity lives within one of the 24 Zones, heavily developed regions controlled by the Monoliths. Outside the Zones lies the Pale, where conditions are much harder for humans to live in. GEOGRAPHY & LIFE While appearing on the surface very similar to earth, Zenith is a strange and diverse planet, with many biomes and ecosystems having no direct Earth equivalent. Some species are harmless and live alongside humans, while others can be dangerous to people and infrastructure. Large portions of the planet remain sparsely explored, particularly outside developed areas. THE ZONES The 24 Zones are the main centers of human civilization on Zenith. Each is governed by a Monolith, which controls its government, infrastructure, and major industries. Zones are heavily managed environments designed to keep their populations safe and comfortable. Each Zone is surrounded by a largely invisible barrier that helps maintain its conditions and limits the movement of contaminants and other environmental factors. THE PALE The Pale refers to the area outside of zones. Refer to the page on The Pale to learn more.

title: AquaFlo
description: The Monolith responsible for water extraction, purification, and distribution throughout Zenith.
text: OVERVIEW The water of Zenith is mildly toxic. It can be safely consumed for short periods, but long-term exposure causes a variety of health problems and can significantly reduce a person's lifespan. AquaFlo is the Monolith responsible for extracting, purifying, and distributing water across Zenith. Its infrastructure includes wells, treatment plants, pipelines, reservoirs, and countless smaller facilities scattered throughout the Zones and Pale. AquaFlo is particularly prominent in Rho, where centuries of water extraction have made the company a major part of the Zone's economy and development. HISTORY AquaFlo was established during the formation of the modern Zones, originally to deal with Zenith's contaminated water. Its early infrastructure was concentrated in what would become Rho, where the company quickly became responsible for much of the region's water supply. As AquaFlo expanded its purification plants and extraction sites, its control over Rho's water infrastructure eventually allowed it to become the Zone's Monolith. The company continued expanding across Zenith over the following centuries. Some of its older water sources have since been exhausted, leaving abandoned facilities scattered throughout Rho. Many have been salvaged or repurposed by locals, while others remain under AquaFlo ownership. AquaFlo's leadership has remained within the same family for generations. CULTURE AquaFlo has a strong sense of hierarchy. The company's ruling family is treated with considerably more respect and ceremony than ordinary employees, and differences in wealth and living conditions are obvious. The company takes considerable pride in its history and presents water management as a responsibility passed down through generations. Many employees genuinely take pride in keeping their communities supplied with clean water, while others are simply there for the stable employment and benefits. Working conditions vary depending on the job. Office positions and specialized careers can be comfortable, while factory, maintenance, and field work can be physically demanding and dangerous. AquaFlo employees often develop strong camaraderie, particularly among workers who spend long periods together at remote facilities or company towns. WORKING FOR AQUAFLO An employee working at Aquaflo might work at a purification plant, travel between monoliths repairing pipelines, or provide security for an isolated facility. More interestingly, many employees are being forced to set out on expeditions to survey The Pale for water sources. Working in and exploring the Pale is dangerous, but positions may come with better pay or benefits. Some employees spend years moving between facilities as the company follows new water sources. RUMORS AquaFlo has kept Zenithians satiated for generations, so many try to not push their luck with the corp. In Rho, where the company's operations have reshaped the land for generations, people have more reasons to be suspicious. The Border: Rho's outskirts seem to change every few years. New extraction sites appear farther into the wasteland, followed by roads, settlements, and company facilities. Some Rhoans wonder how much land the company intends to claim. No Such Thing as Abandoned: Old AquaFlo facilities are scattered throughout Rho, some left behind when their water sources ran dry. There are stories of surveyors returning to these sites years later, taking measurements and marking the surrounding land for unknown reasons. Displacement: Talora communities have been pushed out of areas earmarked for AquaFlo projects. The company insists its operations are lawful, but locals tell stories of settlements abandoned under pressure, sometimes before any official announcement of construction. NOTES AquaFlo CEO is historically titled Lord/Lady [NAME], the Great Purifier of the Waters. The full title still appears on official documents, although most people simply call them the CEO. AquaFlo is one of the oldest continuously operating Monoliths. It is one of the most geographically spread-out Monoliths, with facilities throughout the Zones and Pale. AquaFlo infrastructure can remain operational for generations, with newer systems often built around older facilities. Many Rho settlements originally developed around AquaFlo infrastructure.

title: BioMedica
description: Zenith's largest healthcare corporation and the Monolith responsible for Lamda.
text: OVERVIEW BioMedica is Zenith's largest healthcare corporation and the Monolith responsible for Lamda. Its operations include hospitals, clinics, medical research, healthcare plans, and the manufacture of medical products. BioMedica is known for its medical services and the effectiveness of its treatments. Its hospitals are well-funded, and its research has produced significant medical advancements. Healthcare plans are available at varying levels of cost and coverage. Monolith employees commonly receive healthcare benefits through their employment, making corporate positions particularly attractive. However, coverage can be expensive for lower-income individuals, and uninsured patients face substantially higher costs. HISTORY BioMedica grew through its success in healthcare and medical research. Its hospitals and medical products established its reputation, while its services became increasingly important to the other Monoliths. As more Monoliths began offering BioMedica healthcare plans as an employee benefit, the corporation gained a broad customer base and lasting business relationships. Healthcare coverage became a common employment benefit across corporate Zenith. Many children grow up hearing "Get a job at a Monolith, you'll need the care when you're older!" Its growing resources supported further research and development, allowing BioMedica to expand its medical capabilities and operations throughout the Zones. After the previous Monolith in Lamda, Greenthumb, faced a massive financial crash-- Biomedica swooped in and took their place, the former floundering into a lower level company, and shell of its former self. Lamda now serves as the corporation's primary base and a major center for medical professionals and retirees. WORKING FOR BIOMEDICA Working for BioMedica is considered a respectable career, particularly for doctors, researchers, and other qualified professionals. Not everyone works in medicine. BioMedica also needs administrators, technicians, maintenance staff, factory workers, and other support personnel to keep its operations running. The company has a reputation for high standards and demanding work. Most employees take pride in contributing to medical progress, though the full scope of BioMedica's research is not known to everyone working there. Many staff- From higher to lower, are known to be suddenly 'moved' into other locations, for classified or patented projects. Do too good of a job, and you might just catch the executives eye. CULTURE BioMedica maintains a professional and quiet workplace culture. Employees are expected to meet high standards and maintain the corporation's high reputation for competence. Employment is considered prestigious, particularly for doctors, researchers, and other highly qualified professionals. These positions can offer strong compensation, healthcare benefits, and opportunities for advancement. Many employees take pride in their work and regard medical research as an important contribution to human health. Because of this and the above, The corporation's has very demanding standards and a competitive enviroment. RUMORS BioMedica has a good reputation, and most people have little reason to question it. Still, its size and influence have inspired the occasional rumor. Missing Patients: Every so often, someone claims a relative was transferred to a BioMedica facility and never heard from again. Usually, the patient was already seriously ill, and the paperwork appears to be in order. The Long-Term Residents: Some residents of Lamda's more expensive retirement communities seem to age remarkably well. People joke about unusually good healthcare, though a few insist there's more to it. Private Clinics: BioMedica operates facilities that don't appear in its public directories. Most people assume they're reserved for sensitive research or wealthy clients. Nobody seems to know what actually happens inside. Experimental Treatment: Stories circulate about an experimental procedure that can reverse conditions thought to be permanent. Supposedly, it works. Getting access to it is another matter entirely. The Research Wing: Former low-level employees occasionally allude to research divisions with rules far stricter than the rest of the company. Some claim even senior staff aren't told what their colleagues are working on. The Fine Print: BioMedica's healthcare contracts are extrodinarily long and complex, some say containing containing clauses that most customers never notice or understand until it's too late. Nobody seems to agree on what those clauses actually permit NOTES Healing Foam is one of its best-known medical products and is commonly used by Fixers.

title: Palisade
description: The Monolith responsible for defense manufacturing and security infrastructure across Zenith.
text: OVERVIEW Palisade is the Monolith responsible for defense and security infrastructure across Zenith. It manufactures and weapons and security products used throughout the Zones. Palisade works closely with other Monoliths and corporations, providing the equipment and expertise needed to secure their territories, facilities, and operations. It heavily contributes to the Conglomerate, supplying the Gavel with weapons and tools. Its products are known for their quality, and its services remain widely used despite its reputation for brutality. The company believes that a stable society requires strict laws, effective enforcement, and the suppression of threats and negative ideas. Palisade's approach to security is exceptionally harsh, and its methods are often considered excessive or cruel. The company prioritizes results over public approval, pointing to low crime rates in areas under its protection as evidence of its effectiveness. HISTORY Palisade's history in Eta began with its corporate war against Plastigen, the former Monolith controlling the Zone. Plastigen manufactured plastics using technology that had fallen behind newer materials and manufacturing techniques. Despite its environmentally destructive industry, it maintained relatively permissive laws and generally avoided interfering with private life. Eta developed a distinctive culture centered around nightlife, entertainment, recreational drugs, and unusual fashion. Approximately thirty years ago, Palisade defeated Plastigen and seized control of Eta. Plastigen was dissolved, and its employees were all burnt and killed. Palisade concealed the killings and presented the takeover as the removal of problematic elements from the Zone. Following the takeover, Palisade demolished and rebuilt parts of Eta around its industries. It also expanded more into Tourism, opening Paliland, the largest amusement park in the world. Resistance began within months. Protests, strikes, and civil disobedience escalated into an extended urban uprising known as the Etan Revolt. Palisade killed and imprisoned large numbers of people while suppressing the revolt. Although the major uprising eventually ended, resistance continued through smaller underground movements, some of which developed into smuggling networks and nightlife syndicates. In the following decades, Palisade encouraged wealthy residents and tourists to return to Eta. Redevelopment revitalized parts of the Zone but also raised living costs and displaced poorer residents. CULTURE Palisade's institutional culture emphasizes discipline, effectiveness, and authority. Employees are expected to take security seriously, follow established procedures, and prioritize the organization's objectives. The company values results over public approval. Its position is that strict enforcement is necessary to maintain a functioning society, and that the effectiveness of a security measure matters more than whether it is considered excessive. Although individual employees may take pleasure in cruelty, Palisade's institutional justification for harsh methods is primarily practical: they are acceptable if they achieve the desired outcome. Working for Palisade is closely associated with the defense and security industries. Its employees may work in manufacturing, engineering, surveillance, communications, logistics, security infrastructure, or administrative roles. The company's broad network of contracts creates demand for both technical specialists and industrial workers. WORKING FOR PALISADE Working for Palisade is considered a stable career, particularly in security, research, and technical fields. Despite its strict reputation, the workplace can be surprisingly pleasant. Colleagues are generally friendly, and employees who do their jobs well can genuinely find satisfaction in their careers. Palisade's standards apply to everyone, including its leadership. Unlike some other Monoliths, senior staff are not necessarily exempt from consequences when they make mistakes or violate company rules. Rank carries authority, but it does not guarantee immunity. Employees are expected to meet the same standards of discipline and competence regardless of their position. Palisade is demanding, but its expectations are clear and workers have reason to take pride in meeting them. The company's harsher side tends to emerge when someone challenges its authority or puts its objectives at risk. RUMORS Palisade's reputation for secrecy and excessive enforcement has inspired plenty of rumors, particularly in Eta. Most are difficult to verify, and the company rarely responds to speculation. Children Behind the Walls: Locals near certain Palisade facilities have reported seeing children entering heavily guarded buildings, despite no obvious connection to schools or childcare services. Palisade has offered no public explanation, and the stories remain difficult to confirm. A Different Kind of Soldier: Rumors circulate among security contractors about operatives capable of doing things ordinary training cannot explain. Some attribute the stories to experimental equipment or embellished accounts of classified missions No Room for Defectors: There are persistent stories of Palisade personnel who attempted to leave the company under unusual circumstances, only to have their records sealed or their departures quietly erased. Whether these cases involve ordinary security concerns or something more serious is unclear. The Next Stage: Palisade has long promoted the idea that threats should be stopped before they can cause harm. Recently, some insiders have speculated that the company is developing ways to identify criminal intent itself, rather than simply tracking suspicious behavior. Whether this is a genuine program or corporate advertising remains unclear. Borrowed: Other Monolith employees report their higher ups sometimes receiving specialized Palisade personnel for sensitive assignments. These operatives arrive with unusual restrictions and requirements, answer to handlers outside the borrowing organization, and leave little documentation behind. NOTES Palisade is the defense and security Monolith, supplying weapons, surveillance systems, police equipment, and security infrastructure throughout Zenith. Its products are widely relied upon despite its reputation for brutality. Eta was formerly controlled by Plastigen, a plastics manufacturer, before Palisade seized control approximately thirty years ago.

title: Lamda
description: An affluent, carefully maintained Zone known for its garden cities and Art Deco-inspired architecture. Controlled by the healthcare Monolith, Lamda.
text: OVERVIEW Lamda is a densely populated Zone owned and operated by BioMedica. It is known for its carefully maintained cities, extensive greenery, Art Deco-inspired architecture, and high standard of living. The Zone is home to medical professionals, researchers, corporate employees, retirees, and wealthy residents, alongside the service workers who keep its cities running. Lamda has a reputation for being comfortable, expensive, sheltered, and somewhat snobbish. Lamda's residents benefit from reliable public services and well-maintained surroundings, though this comfort comes with a distinctly corporate and 'old' atmosphere. GEOGRAPHY & INFRASTRUCTURE Lamda is a relatively mild, rainy Zone with a very green landscape. Most developed areas consist of cities and surrounding residential neighborhoods, with gardens, parks, and landscaped streets incorporated throughout. Much of modern Lamda was constructed or redesigned by BioMedica after the collapse of the previous Monolith. The resulting cities follow a garden-city layout with pedestrian-friendly streets, plazas, courtyards, and nature covered walkways. Architecture is distinctly older looking then other zones- Specifically, resembling real world Art Deco constructions. Older and wealthier areas tend to be more ornate, while newer buildings are generally cleaner and more restrained. Cars and buses are available, but walking is a common way to get around. Public facilities are regularly maintained, and security cameras and other monitoring systems are widespread, usually blending into the surrounding architecture. HISTORY Lamda was once a relatively ordinary green region whose economy relied heavily on agriculture, particularly vegetable production. Its former Monolith, Greenthumb, specialized in growing and distributing vegetables, but gradually lost ground as Harvestons production displaced traditional agricultural supply chains. Following a major crisis, the Greenthumb became defunct, slipping off into mere Corporation territory. BioMedica acquired the Zone and began a major redevelopment of its cities, turning Lamda into a headquarters and residential center for doctors, researchers, executives, and other skilled professionals. As BioMedica expanded its retirement services, Lamda also became a major destination for retirees from across Zenith. Retirement communities and elderly care are now important parts of the Zone's population and economy. CULTURE Lamdan culture places considerable value on education, professional achievement, organized social life, and comfortable living. Residents are commonly stereotyped as polite, sheltered, health-conscious, and out of touch with life in poorer Zones. Lamda also has a reputation for being humorless, although its humor tends to be dry, understated, and sarcastic. Professional competence carries considerable prestige. Doctors, researchers, and other skilled workers are generally respected, and career or academic achievements can be a source of personal and family pride. Clubs, societies, and neighborhood organizations are popular ways to socialize. Many residents belong to several groups at once, ranging from professional associations to hobby clubs and recreational societies. Fashion Lamdan fashion tends to be affluent, professional, and coordinated.Expensive or well-made garments often signal social standing without relying on particularly flashy designs. Food & Dining Bread, pastries, soups, sausages, and baked dishes are common, alongside more elaborate local cuisine. Going out to eat is a common way to socialize. Cafes and restaurants are used for dates, meetings, family gatherings, and casual time with friends. Music & Recreation Lamda has a strong classical and orchestral music tradition. Specifically jazz, lounge music, piano performances, and acoustic acts. Organized hobbies are popular throughout the Zone. Gardening, crafts, book groups, music societies, and recreational clubs provide regular social outlets. Retirement communities contribute heavily to this culture, with many activities originally associated with older residents becoming popular across the wider population. Chess is also well established in Lamda, which occasionally hosts notable competitions and has helped give the Zone a reputation for the game. Events & Festivals Garden shows, seasonal festivals, markets, charity events, and neighborhood gatherings are common throughout the year. Retirement communities hold their own dances, games, and hobby events, some of which have become wider Lamdan traditions. BioMedica also hosts medical conventions, research showcases, and corporate celebrations that attract visitors from other Zones. Local Speech Lamdan speech is generally considered close to standard Zenithan, though residents have a reputation for speaking more formally and politely than people from some other Zones. Humor is often dry or understated with lots of sarcasm sprinkled throughout. Outsiders sometimes interpret their reserved style as a lack of humor. DAILY LIFE Most Lamdans live in comfortable apartment complexes or planned residential neighborhoods. Evenings are generally quiet. Restaurants and cafes are popular throughout the zone, and private dinners, club meetings, and smaller social gatherings are vastly more common than any sort of nightlife scene. Lamda is relatively affluent, and residents often have more opportunities to move between jobs, pursue education, and access services than people in poorer Zones. BioMedica employees and retirees may have particular reasons to remain in the Zone for long periods. SUBZONES / DISTRICTS BioMedica District The central corporate and medical district. It contains BioMedica Headquarters, major hospitals, research facilities, corporate offices, and specialist clinics. Garden District Centered around Lamda's major public garden and botanical grounds. Parks, residential neighborhoods, cafes, and other public spaces fill the surrounding area. Retirement District A large area dedicated to retirement communities, assisted living, elderly services, and recreation. Both ordinary and luxury retirement communities can be found here. Resort District Tourism is a secondary part of Lamda's economy, attracting visitors interested in its gardens, healthcare, and comfortable surroundings. Residential Districts The Zone's main residential areas, consisting primarily of comfortable mid-rise apartment buildings, with larger luxury complexes in wealthier neighborhoods. Schools, restaurants, local businesses, and other services are distributed throughout. KEY LOCATIONS BioMedica Headquarters: A large corporate campus consisting of connected buildings, gardens, public spaces, and a central landmark building. Lamda Central Hospital District: The Zone's primary medical center, supported by smaller hospitals and clinics throughout Lamda. Lamda Public Garden: A large botanical garden and public park. Lamda Commercial Districts: Shopping and dining areas containing restaurants, cafes, markets, boutiques, and other businesses. Lamda Chess Venues: Clubs and competition venues used for local and inter-Zone chess events. CREATING A LAMDAN CHARACTER Lamda's population extends well beyond doctors and researchers. A Lamdan character might be a BioMedica employee, a retired worker from another Zone, a student, a restaurant owner, a corporate administrator, a maintenance worker, or someone employed in the tourism and service industries. Characters can come from comfortable professional households or from the lower-income communities that support the Zone's affluent lifestyle. They might take pride in Lamda's safety and amenities, feel constrained by its social expectations, or have little experience with life outside its carefully maintained cities. Someone who grew up in Lamda may be accustomed to reliable healthcare, organized social activities, and well-maintained public spaces. Leaving the Zone can expose them to living conditions and social expectations they have rarely encountered firsthand. TRIVIA Lamda's architecture draws heavily from Art Deco and garden-city design. The public garden is both a major recreational space and a botanical garden. The Zone has a large retirement population, and elderly services are an important part of its economy. Chess competitions have contributed to Lamda's association with the game. Lamdans have a reputation for being clean, polite, and somewhat humorless. The Zone's public facilities are considered among the best maintained on Zenith. Residents who move to Lamda often stay for long periods.

title: Meta
description: About the project and the site
text: ABOUT THIS PROJECT Retrograde began on April 27th, 2023. Since then, it has undergone extensive changes, rewrites, and countless additions. What began as a much smaller project has grown into a far larger and more complex world, with plenty more to explore in the years ahead. In its early stages, Retrograde never had a dedicated wiki. This website aims to change that, with the goal to gather years of artwork, lore, and worldbuilding into a single, accessible reference for the setting. Think of it as a sort of DM guide, A place to understand the world, its characters, and the corporations that shape it. There have also been plans to explore Retrograde through short stories, comics, video games, and animatics. For now, the focus is currently on Retrograde as a TTRPG setting, one that will continue to grow, evolve, and occasionally be rewritten as new ideas take shape. That is to say, anything on this website is subject to change. Thank you for taking the time to view it! 88 X 31 BUTTONS TO-DO's The biggest current priority is adding all 50 characters. Each one is planned to have its own references and artwork, alongside their written profiles, so this will take some time. But it'll get done. Beyond that, there's still plenty of work to do on the setting itself. More Zone pages, Monolith pages, company profiles, institutes, and everything in between are all on the list. For now, the goal is simply to get everything documented and onto the site. CREDITS Retrograde, as a Project and Website, was Written, designed and built by Retrograde on Neocities. Fonts: IBM Plex Sans, Bebas Neue, Tomorrow (All free on Google Fonts) Any External Art or Photography is used as placeholder with full credits/links to their creator where the image is found. Built with HTML, CSS and Eleventy Hosted proudly on Neocities, Backed up on Github. Tested on Linux, Firefox and Chromium. Mobile usage might not be great (for now) USAGE & CONTACT Retrograde is an independently created fictional setting and creative work. Unless otherwise stated, all original text, artwork, characters, designs, and related materials are protected by their respective rights holders. title: Eta
description: A large coastal Zone known for its beaches, nightlife, entertainment, and relaxed local culture. Controlled by the security Monolith, Palisade.
text: OVERVIEW Eta is a large coastal Zone known for its beautiful beaches and nightlife scene. Before being acquired by Palisade, Eta was controlled by Plastigen, a plastics manufacturer. Plastigen was environmentally destructive but maintained relatively permissive laws and largely avoided interfering with private life. Approximately thirty years ago, Palisade defeated Plastigen in a corporate war and took control of Eta. The takeover was followed by mass killings, widespread redevelopment, unemployment, and a violent uprising against the new government. Modern Eta is significantly more expensive and heavily regulated than it was under Plastigen. Despite this, many aspects of its former culture remain through the Etans' stubborn and rebellious attitudes. GEOGRAPHY & INFRASTRUCTURE Eta is a mostly flat coastal region with a large urban population concentrated along the ocean. Much of the Zone consists of one enormous metropolitan area, with more sparsely developed areas extending inland. The climate is warm and humid year-round, with a pronounced rainy season during the summer. Vegetation is more lush around developed areas. The ocean surrounding Eta, like much of Zenith, is mildly toxic but considered safe enough for swimming. Much of Eta's infrastructure predates Palisade. The company repurposed many former Plastigen factories and warehouses, while other areas were demolished and rebuilt. Palisade security infrastructure is highly visible throughout the Zone. Cameras, checkpoints, drones, patrols, warning systems, and other equipment are common in major public districts and are displayed openly and proudly. HISTORY Palisade's history in Eta began with its corporate war against Plastigen, the former Monolith controlling the Zone. Plastigen manufactured plastics using technology that had fallen behind newer materials and manufacturing techniques. Despite its environmentally destructive industry, it maintained relatively permissive laws and generally avoided interfering with private life. Eta developed a distinctive culture centered around nightlife, entertainment, recreational drugs, and unusual fashion. Approximately thirty years ago, Palisade defeated Plastigen and seized control of Eta. Plastigen was dissolved, and its employees were all burnt and killed. Palisade concealed the killings and presented the takeover as the removal of problematic elements from the Zone. Following the takeover, Palisade demolished and rebuilt parts of Eta around its industries. It also expanded more into Tourism, opening Paliland, the largest amusement park in the world. Resistance began within months. Protests, strikes, and civil disobedience escalated into an extended urban uprising known as the Etan Revolt. Palisade killed and imprisoned large numbers of people while suppressing the revolt. Although the major uprising eventually ended, resistance continued through smaller underground movements, some of which developed into smuggling networks and nightlife syndicates. In the following decades, Palisade encouraged wealthy residents and tourists to return to Eta. Redevelopment revitalized parts of the Zone but also raised living costs and displaced poorer residents. CULTURE Etan Appearance Etans are generally somewhat shorter and commonly have straight hair, lighter skin tones, and red/auburn, blonde hair, or brown hair with reddish hues. Narrower facial structures, pointy and 'ratlike' features, and irregular teeth are stereotypical and common amongst Etans. Skin blemishes, scarring, freckles, and other visible imperfections are also more common. Etans are stereotypically considered unattractive by people from other Zones. Fashion Eta is known for flashy and expressive fashion, particularly clothing associated with nightlife and entertainment. Bright colors, bold patterns, jewelry, dramatic accessories, revealing clothing, and unusual combinations are common. Older styles from Eta's pre-Palisade nightlife culture remain influential. Fashion is also used as a form of cultural expression and, at times, deliberate opposition to Palisade and corporate attempts to regulate behavior. Music Eta has a strong association with 'euro'-rave (Europe doesn't exist in Retrograde, but it's for comparison) and electronic music. Food & Drink Etan food is stereotyped (somewhat rightfully) as looking disgusting and strange to outsiders, and being an acquired taste. It tends to favor casual, fried, sauced, and seafood-based dishes. Sweet and savory combos are common, and traditional dishes combine ingredients that appear unusual or unappetizing to outsiders. Fruit, jams, mayonnaise-like sauces, fried seafood, pasta, and other ingredients are frequently combined in unconventional ways. Brightly colored and heavily sweetened drinks are also popular, particularly alongside late-night and beach food. Sports & Festivals Beach sports are popular in Eta. The Zone also hosts commercial festivals such as parades or theme-park celebrations. Large rave festivals continue to occur, but usually stay underground due to Palisade restrictions. Local Speech Eta has one of the most distinctive accents on Zenith and is known for having an unusually large amount of local slang. Guttered - Reported to Palisade. Gobber - A Gavel officer. Under the wire - Avoiding surveillance or getting around a restriction. Drenched - Exhausted, particularly after partying. Gaffed - Causing trouble or making a mess of something. Salti - A native Etan. Fence - A monitored area. Brightside - A sarcastic name for Eta, referring to Palisade's sanitized image of the Zone. Paled - Being forced out of an area by Palisade. Backlight - An underground venue. Glowbug - A partier. Bleached - Something heavily sanitized or regulated by Palisade. Slip - A small act of getting around a restriction. Guttermouth - A snitch. Whistler - A snitch. Bluebell - A suspected informant or undercover agent. Badgekisser - Someone excessively loyal to the Monoliths. Noodle - An idiot, usually in a harmless or humorous sense. Dunter - Someone considered dumb. Dreg - An unpleasant person. Wobbler - Someone who lies frequently or acts cowardly. The following are offensive terms used against Etans: Nightcrawler - Referring to their nightlife culture and 'criminal activity'. Backroomer - Implying that Etans are involved in underground businesses and organized crime. DAILY LIFE Eta has a relatively laid-back social culture. People commonly spend their free time at large malls and entertainment venues. This isn't limited to the rich, either. Poorer residents also regularly attend parties and participate in nightlife using cheaper or informal venues. Palisade's restrictions have reduced the amount of legitimate venues available. Many businesses operate under tightly controlled hours, while underground venues provide alternatives for those willing to take the risk.s SUBZONES / DISTRICTS Central Eta The enormous urban core of Eta. Central Eta contains older neighborhoods, modern high-rises, shopping districts, restaurants, entertainment venues, and much of the Zone's commercial activity. Coastal District The main tourist and recreational area along Eta's coastline. It contains beaches, resorts, boardwalks, waterfront restaurants, and other entertainment businesses. Industrial District An inland industrial area containing factories, warehouses, utilities, logistics infrastructure, and major Palisade facilities. Much of its infrastructure was originally built by Plastigen and later repurposed. Paliland A massive resort and entertainment district centered around Paliland, a large theme park based around an idealized presentation of Zenith. The district contains hotels, restaurants, shops, entertainment venues, transportation infrastructure, and employee housing. It operates under more permissive regulations than most of Eta, including the absence of normal curfews. KEY LOCATIONS Sunburst Boardwalk - A famous coastal destination containing beaches, shops, restaurants, entertainment, and other tourist attractions. Marquee District - A former nightlife district heavily damaged during the takeover and uprising. Large portions remain abandoned and are now used for underground parties, illegal venues, smuggling, and other criminal activity. MetaMall - A huge shopping and entertainment complex. Palisade Complex - Palisade's primary facility, a large walled-off area containing offices, warehouses, and other facilities. Paliland - Eta's enormous corporate-sponsored theme-park resort. CREATING AN ETAN CHARACTER Eta's population includes everyone from tourism and entertainment workers to independent business owners to- yes of course- criminals. An Etan might run a beachside restaurant, perform at clubs, participate in underground fight clubs, or simply live an ordinary life in the Zone. Characters may have grown up in Eta before Palisade's takeover, though if theyre younger then thirty they've likely lived their entire lives under its control. Someone who grew up in Eta may be accustomed to its expressive fashion, distinctive slang, and laid-back social culture. However, life under Palisade has made open rebellion increasingly risky, and not everyone can afford to resist. Some Etans find ways to preserve their culture underground, while others have adapted to the new order or feel little connection to the Zone's past. TRIVIA MetaMall has remained a major social destination across multiple generations. Paliland's giant Zenith globe is deliberately inaccurate and primarily decorative. Paliland completely omits the Eta Revolt from its presentation of Eta's history. Obviously

title: Timeline
description: A Timeline for Retrograde (Subject to change)
text: The Exodus Era Year 0 Humanity abandons Earth after centuries of environmental collapse. The Colonial Era Year 1–30 Hundreds of colony ships arrive on Zenith, establishing settlements across the planet. Year 8 The earliest permanent human settlements are established. Year 40–80 Humans begin documenting Zenith's unfamiliar flora and fauna. Year 70–95 Growing competition over land, resources, and trade creates tensions between human settlements. The Great Zenith War Year 96 Open warfare breaks out between competing human factions. Year 110 Researchers discover that the powerful native creatures later known as Moon Children possess highly energetic internal cores. Year 130 The first Signature is created from a stabilized Moon Child core. Year 130–180 Signatures are developed and used by competing factions. Moon Children are hunted extensively for their cores. Year 188 The First Human War ends after decades of conflict, leaving much of early human civilization destroyed. The Unity Era Year 190–250 Human settlements rebuild and reorganize following the war. Year 215–280 Knowledge of Signature creation becomes increasingly fragmented and eventually lost. Year 300 The last known Moon Children are believed to have been killed. Year 320 Moon Children are considered extinct, making new Signatures impossible to create. The Zone Era Year 330–380 Major settlements begin developing large-scale environmental control systems to protect their populations from Zenith's wilderness. Year 360 The earliest recognizable Zones are established. Year 370–450 Zones expand and their governments gain increasing political and economic authority. Year 440 Several Zone governments begin developing into the organizations that will eventually become the Monoliths. The Enterprise Era Year 460–550 The emerging Monoliths consolidate control over major industries, infrastructure, and government. Year 570–700 Monolith-controlled companies expand beyond their home Zones, bringing major industries under increasingly centralized corporate control. Year 650–700 The 24 Monoliths become the dominant political and economic powers on Zenith. The Monolithic Era Year 700–850 Monoliths expand their influence over transportation, communications, healthcare, education, manufacturing, and other major industries. Year 820–880 Inter-Zone transportation, communication, and commerce become increasingly important. Year 850–900 The Monolith system becomes deeply established across Zenith. The Terminal Era Year 900 The social, economic, and political systems recognizable in modern Zenith become firmly established. Year 930–980 Continued industrial development causes increasing environmental damage outside the Zones. Year 950 The Pale becomes increasingly difficult for ordinary humans to inhabit. Year 999 Year 999 Signs of instability begin to emerge around the Zone barriers.

title: Rho
description: A vast, sparsely populated badlands and canyons with a Wild West flavor. Controlled by AquaFlo, the industrial water producing Monolith.
text: OVERVIEW Rho is a sparsely populated Zone ravaged by its water industry and Monolith AquaFlo. Much of the Zone consists of dry plains, red sandstone, deep canyons, and mesas. Most settlements are small and separated by long stretches of undeveloped land. Water extraction has been one of Rho's defining industries for centuries. The Zone is an important source of water for the rest of Zenith, although the wealth generated by the industry is not evenly distributed. GEOGRAPHY & INFRASTRUCTURE Rho's terrain is mostly dry and sun-baked, with sparse vegetation outside areas near settlements and reliable water sources. Large industrial facilities are scattered throughout the Zone, particularly water extraction, purification, storage, and distribution facilities. Some of these complexes are enormous, with machinery built directly into the surrounding terrain. Rho also has a large network of smaller settlements. Some are old communities that have existed for generations, while others grew around industrial facilities. HISTORY Rho's earliest human settlements were established as prisoner and slave colonies, originally used for quarrying and extracting stone and construction materials. Over generations, their descendants developed into the Talora, forming a distinct culture and identity. Water extraction eventually became Rho's dominant industry. As the industry expanded, Talora communities were gradually displaced by extraction facilities, pipelines, reservoirs, roads, and new settlements. Rho has experienced periods of prosperity because of its water industry, but much of that wealth has historically remained concentrated around the companies and communities closest to the industry. CULTURE Rho has a strong regional identity, and Rhoans generally take pride in their culture despite widespread stereotypes about the Zone. Rhoan culture is influenced by frontier traditions, Southern influences, vehicle culture, and a strong emphasis on self-sufficiency. Rhoans tend to be skeptical of outsiders, particularly people from wealthier or more urban Zones. Older technology and traditional customs are often embraced rather than discarded. Repairing, modifying, and reusing things is common, and practical skills are highly valued. Appearance Rhoans commonly have tan to medium-brown skin, brown or dark brown hair, and soft facial features with relatively broad or flat proportions. Wavy and curly hair is common, as is facial hair among adults who grow it. These traits vary considerably between individuals and are not universal among Rhoans. Fashion Rhoan clothing tends to be practical, durable, and loose-fitting, particularly because of the climate and the Zone's industrial and agricultural lifestyle. Workwear such as cargo pants, coveralls, utility vests, boots, gloves, and oversized jackets is common. Clothing is often modified with pockets, straps, tools, or other equipment. Outside of workwear, Rhoan fashion has strong streetwear and motorsport influences. Graphic jackets, racing-inspired clothing, cropped tops, loose trousers, caps, and customized garments are common. Bright colors, particularly orange, red, yellow, and blue, are popular as accents and statement pieces. Secondhand, repaired, and repurposed clothing is also widespread. Vehicle Culture Vehicles are deeply embedded in Rhoan life. The distance between settlements makes them necessary, while racing and vehicle modification are popular forms of recreation. Rho is known throughout Zenith for heavily modified vehicles, off-road racing, and unusual custom builds. Racing takes place both informally and through organized events, and major races and vehicle shows are frequently filmed in the Zone. Music Rho has a recognizable musical tradition that is considered older and more traditional than the music of many urban Zones. Its continued popularity is partly attributed to Rho's isolation and the importance placed on preserving local culture. Food & Drink Rhoan cuisine is heavily inspired by Southern American comfort food. Strong spices, sauces, rubs, and seasoning are common. Fresh ingredients and home cooking are culturally important. Depending on the settlement, gardens, livestock, hunting, and other small-scale food production may supplement imported food. Rho also has a strong culture of locally produced alcohol. Homemade drinks are often particularly strong and pungent. Sports & Festivals Dustball is a popular Rhoan sport loosely descended from soccer. Different communities maintain their own variations. The largest annual festival is the Dustrink, which combines Dustball, racing, food, music, drinking, and other local traditions. The festival is primarily community-run, and Monolith involvement has historically been limited. Local Speech Rhoan speech has its own regional slang. Longhaul: A long-distance trip, particularly between distant settlements. Tin: An old vehicle or piece of machinery. Dry luck: Bad luck or an unfortunate situation. Company town: A settlement dominated by Monolith infrastructure and employment. Pipe Rat: Someone who works around or for the water Monolith. Can also be used dismissively toward Monolith employees. Pipe Mouse: The child of a Pipe Rat, or someone who grew up around the Monolith without working for it. Dusting: Driving or riding around without a particular destination. Burnout: Someone who spends most of their money on gambling, racing, and related hobbies. Junkblood: A self-proclaimed title used by people who build, repair, or modify things from scrap. Some terms are also used against Rhoans by outsiders. Rusty, Canyon Rat, Tanker, and Outback are derogatory terms associated with stereotypes of Rhoans as poor, isolated, or backwards. DAILY LIFE Most Rhoans live in small settlements rather than large cities. Daily life generally revolves around work, family, local businesses, and community activities. Repairing vehicles, machinery, buildings, and household goods is common. Mechanics, fabricators, and other skilled tradespeople are important members of many communities. Water availability varies between settlements. Larger cities and industrial communities generally have reliable supplies, while remote communities may depend on wells, storage systems, or water deliveries. Bars, diners, garages, shops, and private homes commonly serve as gathering places. Education is generally less well-funded than in wealthier Zones. Rho has several trade schools and one university in its main industrial area, although residents seeking specialized education often leave the Zone. Fixing is also particularly common. Rho's isolation and limited law-enforcement coverage make it a common starting point and temporary base for Fixers. SUBZONES / DISTRICTS Industrial District Rho's primary administrative and industrial center. It contains the largest concentration of Monolith offices, corporate infrastructure, major water facilities, and industrial employment, along with a relatively small city. Badlands District The largest and least-developed part of Rho. It consists primarily of barren wilderness, abandoned infrastructure, remote roads, isolated water sources, mines, workshops, and scattered settlements. Monolith services and Gavel presence are more limited here. Historical District The districts containing Rho's established towns and communities, including older settlements and newer communities built around industrial facilities. KEY LOCATIONS The Industrial District: Rho's largest concentration of corporate infrastructure, industry, businesses, and employment. Major Water Facilities: Large extraction, purification, storage, and distribution complexes operated by AquaFlo. Frontier Towns: Numerous small settlements spread throughout the Zone. Dustball Grounds: Local and regional sporting grounds found throughout the Zone. Racing Grounds: Organized tracks and open areas used for professional and amateur racing. CREATING A RHOAN CHARACTER A character from Rho could come from a small frontier settlement, an industrial company town, or one of the Zone's larger communities. Common backgrounds include water-industry workers, mechanics, racers, tradespeople, Fixers, and people involved in local businesses. Rhoans are often familiar with long-distance travel, vehicle maintenance, practical repair work, and making do with limited resources. Someone from a wealthier or more urban Zone may find Rho's culture old-fashioned, while a Rhoan may see those same people as sheltered or overly dependent on corporate infrastructure. TRIVIA Rho is the largest source of processed water for the rest of Zenith. Vehicle and racing programs frequently use Rho as a filming location because of its open terrain. Some Rhoan communities maintain buildings and machinery that have been repaired or modified for generations. Locally produced alcohol is often considered unusually strong by people from other Zones. Rho's major annual festival has historically remained independent of Monolith sponsorship. Rhoans generally have a higher degree of practical mechanical and self-sufficiency skills than outsiders.

title: What is Retrograde?
text: RETROGRADE is a retro-futurist science-fiction world of walled cities, rival corporations, and the people caught between them. Welcome to Zenith! [intro unchanged] The World Zenith is an alien, Earth-like planet divided into 24 Zones. Each Zone belongs to a megacorporation called a Monolith, and each Monolith has total control over its territory. It writes the laws, and nothing happens inside its borders without its knowledge. Rebellion gets crushed quickly, because the status quo is the whole business. Beyond the law, Monoliths run daily life: housing, employment, and education all go through them, and the best amenities are often reserved for employees and their families. A Monolith earns its place by dominating the market until its products are nearly impossible to live without, and by eliminating competitors by whatever means necessary. Replacing one is a monumental event that may happen only once a century. Together, the 24 Monoliths form the Conglomerate, a collective authority that handles matters affecting Zenith as a whole. Its members fight constantly, but none can survive without the others, and that tension is felt across the planet. Daily Life Most people on Zenith live ordinary lives. They go to work, raise families, and keep up their hobbies. The difference is how much money decides what's possible. The universal currency is the Unit, which comes in paper, token, and digital forms. Wealth shapes everything about your life. The rich get spacious houses and penthouses, while the poor might live in an apartment the size of a closet. Even basics like food, water, and healthcare range from extravagant to nonexistent depending on what you can pay. Law is enforced by the Gavel, an institute shared by the Conglomerate that polices every Zone. It is badly understaffed and widely seen as corrupt and incompetent. For those at the very bottom, with nothing to their name and no way to provide for themselves, there is exile. They can be forced out into the Pale, the uninhabitable land outside the Zones, and many don't survive it. Fixers Not everyone wants to spend their life working for a corporation. Some can't get hired in the first place. Others would rather take their chances working for themselves. Fixers are independent contractors who take jobs from people, businesses, and organizations. The work varies wildly. One day you might be tracking down a missing person; the next, smuggling cargo through the Pale, sabotaging a rival company, or helping someone with a problem they'd rather keep quiet. It isn't a stable career. Jobs are dangerous, clients are unreliable, and getting paid is never guaranteed. Some Fixers specialize, while others take whatever comes their way. Fixers can work alone or join a Network, a group that connects contractors, shares resources, and organizes jobs. Networks vary in size, influence, and reputation. Some operate openly, some work in the shadows, and plenty fall somewhere in between. It's not an easy way to make a living, but at least nobody gets to call you into the office on your day off. Probably. Signatures Signatures are extraordinarily rare, anomalous weapons made from the cores of powerful, extinct creatures known as "Moon children." They were created early in Zenith's history and used in the Great War, where many were lost and scattered across the planet. Finding one is about as likely as winning the lottery, if not less. Some believe they are still awake. A Signature will not let anyone use it except its chosen wielder, known as a Signer, and no two are alike. Each has its own abilities, appearance, and personality, and learning to use one takes time. Signers are in demand. Monoliths and Fixers seek them out for their power, and thieves hunt them for their weapons, so many keep their Signature secret. Where to Start Zenith is a big place with a lot of secrets. Pick a topic on the header, or check out one of these: Lore: Everything about the setting. The Monoliths: The Megacoporations and what they do. The Zones: The various places to visit.
